hero.headline: Is It For Real?
hero.subline: Two tools: practice spotting manipulation, or get through the next ten minutes if a fake of someone you know is already circulating.

explainer.body: IsItFR is two tools, kept apart on purpose. Practice puts you inside the trick instead of asking you to define it. Get help is for the minute a fake of someone you know is already circulating.
You can explain media literacy and still freeze when a clip looks like a classmate. A definition does not tell you what to do in that minute, and most advice assumes you have time to study.

You run short experiments without being told what they score. If it is happening now, you follow five fixed steps — stop, save what you saw, choose who to tell, send a message, get resources. That path never asks you to sign in.

entries.body: Try experiments that put you inside the trick. You will need an account.
Stop, save evidence, choose who to tell, send a message. No account. Works offline after the first visit.

footer.note: Crisis help never asks you to sign in.
